forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Stroud held £100.7m of borrowing, all from a government lender, and £33.9m of investments at 30 June 2026
news_drafts.lead:
Stroud District Council had borrowed £100.7m at 30 June 2026, and all of it was owed to the Public Works Loan Board (PWLB), the government's lending arm for councils, run by the Treasury. The figure comes from a schedule of investment and borrowing in the papers for the Audit and Standards Committee meeting of 27 October.

The schedule lists one borrowing line, the PWLB, and no other lenders. Its total reads "TOTAL BORROWING £100,717", in thousands of pounds.

The council's investments at the same date were £33.9m. The schedule shows these separately and groups them as specified investments, property funds and multi-asset funds.
news_drafts.paper_title: Appendix C Schedule of Investment and Borrowing as at 30 June 2026

news_drafts.headline: Stroud council owed £100.717m at 30 June 2026; its next loan repayment, £6m, falls due in March 2032
news_drafts.lead:
Stroud District Council had £100.717m of external borrowing at 30 June 2026, the end of the first quarter of its financial year. The next loan it must repay, £6m, is not due until March 2032, more than five years after the date of the figures. They come from the quarter's treasury management report (how a council borrows, invests its spare cash and manages the risks of both), which went to the Audit and Standards Committee on 29 September.

The council also intends to use internal borrowing of £36.690m to pay for its capital programme, its planned spending on long-lasting assets such as buildings, roads and equipment. Internal borrowing means paying for that spending from the council's own money put aside, rather than taking out a loan. That saves interest but uses up some of the cushion.

The report sets out the council's borrowing position in a table and states the March 2032 repayment as the next on its schedule.

findings.paper_title: Appendix E Managed Funds Update at 30 June 2026
findings.headline: Estimated uncrystallised capital loss on multi-asset investments is £0.075m at 30 June 2026, on initial purchases of £4.000m.
findings.detail: Royal London's current market value is £2.983m against a £3.000m purchase value, and CCLA's is £0.942m against £1.000m. The table's loss column is headed £k, but its values reconcile to the £m columns, so the total is read as £0.075m. The paper does not say how this loss would be funded.
findings.matters: A finance director with multi-asset or pooled fund holdings can compare how a modest unrealised loss sits alongside the reserve set aside for property funds.
findings.figures: £4.000m initial purchase value; £3.925m current market value; £0.075m estimated capital loss at 30/06/26 (Royal London £0.017m, CCLA £0.058m)
findings.quote: Estimated uncrystallised capital loss of Multi-Asset investments is shown in Table 5B

findings.paper_title: Appendix E Managed Funds Update at 30 June 2026
findings.headline: The Investment Risk Reserve is estimated at £208k at 30 June 2026 after £81k of uncrystallised property fund losses are charged to it.
findings.detail: The reserve stood at £289k at 1 April 2026, after crystallised losses. The estimated uncrystallised losses of £66k on Lothbury and £15k on Hermes can be met from the reserve, and the paper expects no impact on the general fund outturn.
findings.matters: A finance director can see how an earmarked reserve funded from past investment income is being drawn down to absorb property fund losses without touching the general fund.
findings.figures: £289k opening balance; £81k estimated uncrystallised loss (£66k Lothbury, £15k Hermes); £208k estimated closing balance at 30 June 2026; £177k crystallised Hermes loss
findings.quote: This can be funded within the existing reserve and so there is no expectation of any impact on the general fund outturn position.

findings.paper_title: Appendix E Managed Funds Update at 30 June 2026
findings.headline: Hermes Property Fund repaid £1,808,894.38 on 18 August 2025, crystallising a £177k capital loss in 2025/26 against a £2m initial investment.
findings.detail: The fund was terminated, and the July 2025 valuation showed a unit price of 6.087. Hermes is holding back a £15k retention to keep the fund vehicle open for tax purposes, and any residual funds will be distributed later. Dividends of £390,341.81 had been received by 31 March 2026, and no further dividends are due.
findings.matters: The paper shows the realised loss on a terminated fund, with a retention still outstanding, which is the pattern finance officers face when closing out a property fund.
findings.figures: £2m initial investment; £1,808,894.38 repayment received 18 August 2025; £177k crystallised loss; £15k retention; £390,341.81 dividends received to 31 March 2026
findings.quote: A capital loss of £177k was crystalised in 2025/26 and charged to the Investment Risk Reserve, as set out in Section 3.

findings.paper_title: Appendix E Managed Funds Update at 30 June 2026
findings.headline: Lothbury Property Fund has sold all its assets, with a final capital loss of £66k estimated for 2026-27 against a £4m initial investment.
findings.detail: The fund was terminated after a large percentage of investors redeemed, and the Council's final repayment received in the period to 30 June 2026 was £8,648.49. Dividends of £525,702.92 had been received by 31 March 2026, and no further dividends are due in 2026/27.
findings.matters: A finance director holding a terminated property fund can compare this capital loss, charged to an earmarked reserve, with how their own reserves would absorb a similar loss.
findings.figures: £4m initial investment; £66k estimated final loss in 2026-27; £8,648.49 final repayment; £525,702.92 dividends received to 31 March 2026
findings.quote: All Fund assets have now been sold.

findings.paper_title: Appendix B – Recommendation Monitoring – Recommendations Exceeded Implementation Date
findings.headline: Legend leisure system integration for general transactions has been fully implemented, while the Direct Debit membership fee link to Unit 4 remains in testing, delayed by ICT resourcing.
findings.detail: The July 2025 audit asked for a financial interface between the Legend and Unit 4 systems for monthly Direct Debit membership fees, with a target of 31/01/2026. The August 2026 update reports the general transactions part complete and the gym membership integration still in testing.
findings.matters: Income collection through a leisure management system feeding the financial ledger is a common reconciliation weakness, and the ICT dependency is a delivery constraint other councils with similar systems will recognise.
findings.quote: The project to integrate the Legend leisure management system for general transactions has been fully implemented
